from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching content from storyboard
        title_text = "Visualizing Convolution: The 'Flip and Slide'"
        lecture_lines = [
            "For continuous variables, we use the 'Flip and Slide'.",
            "One PDF stays still while the other is flipped.",
            "The flipped PDF slides across the stationary one.",
            "The overlapping area calculates the new probability density.",
            "Watch as two squares convolve into a triangle shape."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        GREEN = "#00FF00"
        MAGENTA = "#FF00FF"
        RED = "#FF0000"
        YELLOW = "#FFFF00"
        WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Two rectangular PDF blocks
        green_block = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=1.0, fill_opacity=0.5, color=GREEN, fill_color=GREEN)
        magenta_block = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=1.0, fill_opacity=0.5, color=MAGENTA, fill_color=MAGENTA)
        
        # Positioning: Green at B3, Magenta at B5
        self.place_at_grid(green_block, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(magenta_block, "B5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(green_block), FadeIn(magenta_block))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        
        # Mirror the magenta block horizontally and change its color to red
        # A horizontal flip is a reflection across the vertical axis (UP)
        self.play(
            magenta_block.animate.flip(UP),
            magenta_block.animate.set_color(RED).set_fill(RED),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        red_block = magenta_block # Reference updated for semantics
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        
        # Set up a ValueTracker to control the offset relative to the green block's center
        # Initial position of red_block at D5 relative to green_block at D3 is offset +2.0
        offset_tracker = ValueTracker(2.0)
        
        # Red block follows the tracker
        red_block.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(green_block.get_center() + RIGHT * offset_tracker.get_value()))
        
        # Slide to the left of the green block to prepare for convolution
        self.play(offset_tracker.animate.set_value(-1.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Overlap highlight: calculates the intersection of two 1x1 squares
        def get_overlap():
            x1 = green_block.get_center()[0]
            x2 = red_block.get_center()[0]
            l1, r1 = x1 - 0.5, x1 + 0.5
            l2, r2 = x2 - 0.5, x2 + 0.5
            ol, or_ = max(l1, l2), min(r1, r2)
            if or_ > ol:
                w = or_ - ol
                return Rectangle(
                    width=w, height=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, 
                    color=YELLOW, fill_color=YELLOW, stroke_width=0
                ).move_to([(ol + or_) / 2, green_block.get_center()[1], 0])
            return VMobject() # Return an empty VMobject if no overlap

        overlap_rect = always_redraw(get_overlap)
        self.add(overlap_rect)
        
        # Move until the overlap just starts
        self.play(offset_tracker.animate.set_value(-1.0), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # The triangle curve trackers
        # Place the base line in the lower grid area (Row E)
        base_y = self.grid["E3"][1] - 0.5 
        
        # Base axis for the triangle
        base_line = Line(
            start=[self.grid["E1"][0], base_y, 0],
            end=[self.grid["E6"][0], base_y, 0],
            color=WHITE, stroke_width=1
        )
        self.add(base_line)

        # Trace point calculates the triangle height (overlap area) at current offset
        def get_trace_point():
            off = offset_tracker.get_value()
            area = max(0, 1 - abs(off))
            # The horizontal axis of the convolution plot tracks the sliding block's center
            return np.array([red_block.get_center()[0], base_y + area, 0])

        trace_dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(get_trace_point(), radius=0.01, color=WHITE))
        # TracedPath will draw the triangle as the dot moves
        path = TracedPath(trace_dot.get_center, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        self.add(path, trace_dot)
        
        # Slide through the entire range to trace the triangle distribution
        self.play(offset_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)
